hits.full_text:
All you have to do is commit for 6 months.

That's not a lot. It's actually very little.

6 months is 1% of 50 years, and most people can't stick to something that will change the trajectory of their life for 2 weeks.
hits.hook: thedankoe: commit for 6 months / 1% of 50 years (time-horizon commitment; soften into one small daily thing)
hits.draft_en:
Six months sounds long until you remember how fast a year disappears.

I'm not locking in a new personality. Just one small thing, most days, for half a year.

A page. A walk. Showing up at the desk even when the day is already sideways.

That's the whole plan.
hits.video_tip: 18 seconds, desk, natural light, room sound. A closed notebook. Hand writes today's date, then one short line. Flip back a few pages — same small habit, different days. Last frame text: 'Six months. One line.'

reply_ideas.reply_text: Six months feels honest when the unit is small. One page most days. One walk without the phone. I'm less interested in a new identity than in not quitting the quiet thing.
The 1% math is what got me. Half a year stops sounding dramatic when you picture how fast the last one went. Starting smaller than feels respectable.
Saving this for a walk. Random Show episode titles always sound like a junk drawer in the best way — books next to whatever else Kevin dragged in. Listening with a pen out.
Internal competition is the only scoreboard I can stand lately. Quieter. Less comparing. Just slightly better than yesterday is enough.
